Subject: Post-call: PII handling confirmation / Acme Health

Hi Alicia  thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on next steps: 

Summary of what you said on the call:
- Use case: clinical-summarization assistant for care coordination.
- Data you'll send in prompts: patient name, MRN, short clinical notes (free text).
- Goal: ensure PHI is handled per Acme security policy; data must remain in US-only regions; retention max 90 days; security team needs confirmation on which artifacts are stored (prompts, outputs, logs) and for how long.

Questions I wanted to confirm (so we send the right technical answers to your security team):
1) Is the retention SLA strictly "no more than 90 days" for all logs and prompt text?
2) Do you need redaction at the API layer (we offer client-side redaction helpers) or is server-side opt-out of logging sufficient?
3) Any required certifications / evidence beyond SOC 2 Type II (you mentioned compliance with internal risk standards)?

Initial next steps from our side:
- I attached our redwood-data-retention.pdf (summary)  it covers default hosted behavior and enterprise retention options.
- I'll loop in our security lead (Vivek) and AE (Nikhil) to provide concrete answers about storage location, retention configuration, and available controls (redaction, encryption, private deployment options).
- Proposed: 30-min technical call w/ your security team next week to confirm the config. Does Tue 3/24 or Wed 3/25 work?

Thanks — I want to make sure we give Acme the exact guarantees you need.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII handling confirmation / Acme Health

Thanks Neha  appreciate the recap. Quick answers from our side: 
- Retention: yes, company policy is max 90 days for any logs or persisted PII. For billing/metrics-only aggregates that's fine, but raw prompt text and generated summaries must not be retained beyond 90 days.
- Data types: patient name, MRN (PHI), DOB (partial), and clinical notes  all considered PHI.
- Residency: US-only (we'd prefer east coast region if you can specify).
- Redaction: we'd like server-side options so our product team can send full prompts securely without having to implement client-side redaction immediately.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is baseline; our security team will ask for a short evidence packet and answers to a handful of technical questions (I'll send their questionnaire).

If you can share a short doc that explicitly states: what is stored by default (prompts, outputs, logs), where (region), and retention by artifact type (prompt_text, output_text, request_logs, billing_metrics), that would help our security review.

Tue 3/24 morning works for a technical call. Please include Vivek and Nikhil.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product Security, Acme Health
agomez@acmehealth.com

Attachment: Acme_Security_Questions.xlsx (security team's questionnaire)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII handling confirmation / Acme Health

Alicia  thanks, that is super clear and helpful. Looping in Vivek (our Head of Security) for the detailed answers; below is an initial platform-level summary to address the items you asked about. Vivek, feel free to add or correct.

High-level (Hosted API, enterprise org options):
- What is stored by default:
  - prompt_text: stored in secure logs for up to 30 days by default (used for debugging, quality, safety).
  - output_text: stored for up to 30 days by default.
  - request_logs/metadata (timestamps, IP, model id): stored 90 days by default for enterprise customers, configurable.
  - billing_metrics/aggregates: stored indefinitely as anonymized aggregates for billing and usage analytics.

- Region/residency:
  - Hosted: you can opt into US-only tenancy; logs and artifacts are stored in customer-dedicated buckets in us-east-1 (we can confirm specific AZs for contracts).
  - Dedicated/Private deployments: full control over region and physical hosting (on-prem or VPC).

- Retention controls & redaction:
  - Enterprise orgs can configure a data_retention_policy per-app: you can set prompt_text retention TTL to 0/30/90 days. Setting TTL=0 means prompts are not persisted (ephemeral path).
  - Server-side redaction: we offer configurable pattern-based redaction and a client-side SDK with PII helpers.

- Encryption & access:
  - TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest.
  - Customer-managed KMS keys available for Private/Dedicated customers; hosted customers can request CMKs for enterprise contracts.
  - Audit logs for operator access available for 90 days (longer retention is an add-on).

Attachments: I have attached a short retention summary (redwood-data-retention.pdf). I'll also attach a SOC 2 summary and a small config snippet showing how to set TTLs. 

Next steps:
1) Vivek  can you add any specifics about default retention windows and confirm the storage region behavior for hosted enterprise orgs?
2) Alicia  if 90 days for prompt_text is a firm requirement, we can propose a hosted-enterprise config that sets prompt_text TTL to 90 days and includes a statement in the security addendum.
3) Schedule the tech call Tue 3/24 10:00 AM ET with your security team  confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf, data-retention-config-snippet.txt

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII handling confirmation / Acme Health

Hi Alicia  quick technical confirmation from our side, high level and actionable: 

1) Storage by artifact (hosted enterprise config we recommend):
   - prompt_text: configurable TTL. For Acme we can set TTL=90 days (policy enforced at ingestion). If you require non-persistence, TTL=0 will ensure prompt text is not stored beyond ephemeral memory.
   - output_text: same retention policy as prompt_text (configurable per-app).
   - request_logs/metadata: kept 90 days by default; can be reduced to 30 days on request.
   - billing aggregates: anonymized, retained for billing reconciliation (contact Nikhil for reporting windows).

2) Region/residency:
   - For hosted enterprise customers we will pin storage to us-east-1. We store artifacts in customer-dedicated S3 buckets with access controls and encryption. For contractual language we can specify region=us-east-1.

3) Controls & evidence:
   - Server-side redaction: pattern-based redaction pipelines are available and can be applied at ingestion.
   - Encryption: TLS + AES-256 at rest; support for customer-managed KMS for enterprise.
   - Auditability: operator access logs and KMS access logs are available; we can produce a short evidence packet.

4) Implementation notes for your engineers:
   - To set retention: data_retention_policy: {"prompt_text_ttl_days":90, "request_log_ttl_days":90} (we'll provide exact API snippet in the tech call).
   - KV cache: not persisted to long-term storage in hosted mode; in Dedicated/Private deployments you control persistence.

5) Attachments: I've attached SOC2-Summary.pdf (controls) and a short config snippet you can hand to your infra team (data-retention-config-snippet.txt).

Alicia  confirm Tue 3/24 10:00 AM ET and I'll join the call. If there's a formal questionnaire, please send it over and we'll provide answers ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf, data-retention-config-snippet.txt
